:::{#thm-cramer-rao}
#### Cramér--Rao lower bound

Under the assumptions of @exr-cov-estimator-score,
suppose the [expected information](intro-MLEs.qmd#def-einf) satisfies $0 < \einf(\param) < \infty$.
Then every unbiased estimator $T$ of $\param$ has variance at least
the reciprocal of the expected information:

$$
\Var{T} \ge \frac{1}{\einf(\param)}
$$ {#eq-cramer-rao}

:::

::: proof

The score has variance $\einf(\param) > 0$ by [the theorem on the mean and variance of the score](intro-MLEs.qmd#thm-information-equality),
and $\Covs{T}{\score} = 1$ by @lem-cov-estimator-score.
A constant has covariance zero with every random variable,
so $\Var{T} > 0$.
The [correlation](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/variance-covariance.html#def-correlation)
of $T$ and the score is therefore defined,
and by [its bounds](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/variance-covariance.html#thm-cor-bounds)
its square is at most 1:

$$
\begin{aligned}
1
&\ge \sqf{\Cors{T}{\score}}
&& \text{(correlation lies in $[-1, 1]$)}\\
&= \frac{\sqf{\Covs{T}{\score}}}{\Var{T}\,\Var{\score}}
&& \text{(definition of correlation, squared)}\\
&= \frac{1^2}{\Var{T}\,\einf(\param)}
&& \text{(covariance of $T$ with the score is 1, and the score has variance $\einf(\param)$)}\\
&= \frac{1}{\Var{T}\,\einf(\param)}
&& \text{($1^2 = 1$)}
\end{aligned}
$$

Multiplying both sides by $\Var{T}$ and dividing by $\einf(\param)$,
both positive, gives @eq-cramer-rao.

:::
